digest.key_takeaway:
You've seen it. The first hour with an AI assistant is great. By message 200 it suggests a fix you already rejected, forgets the framework you're using, and confidently reintroduces a bug from an hour ago.

That's context rot, and it's not your imagination.


  
  
  What's going on


Every model has a limited context window. Long chats fill it with everything: dead ends, abandoned approaches, old versions of the same file. Even when it all technically fits, the model has to decide what matters, and old noise competes with the new signal.

articles.title: Check digits explained: how barcodes catch a typo with one number
articles.summary:
Every EAN-13 and UPC-A barcode ends in a digit that isn't data at all. It's a check digit, and it lets a scanner (or your code) reject most typos instantly.


  
  
  The EAN-13 rule


Take the first 12 digits. Multiply them alternately by 1 and 3, starting with 1 from the left. Add it all up. The check digit is whatever brings the total up to the next multiple of 10.

Example: 400638133393?



digits:  4 0 0 6 3 8 1 3 3 3 9 3
weights: 1 3 1 3 1 3 1 3 1 3 1 3
sum = 4+0+0+18+3+24+1+9+3+9+9+9 = 89
check = (10 - 89 % 10) % 10 = 1






So the full code is 4006381333931.
